framing: The 12 REMAINING open questions for Phase 8, after the 2026-07-27 founder-debate resolved pricing, occupancy, and the headcount cap. v1 group bookings = SINGLE-PAYER (organizer pays for all pax) + EXCLUSIVE-only lock, so the whole feature stays inside the existing hold-until-session rail and the GiST exclusion constraint. Pricing is pax-scaled at booking (base + max(0, pax - included) * extraHeadFee, fee defaults 0) but still one payer, NOT per-attendee collection. The RSVP shell is coordination + fraud-corroboration + the foundation the future organizer-driven cost-split (GPAY-01) plugs into. Every question below is HOW to build that shell. RESOLVED & removed from this sheet: the headcount-cap cluster (Q-05..Q-09) and Q-18 — see .planning/HANDOFF.json.

questions.title: Invite delivery mechanism
questions.context: GROUP-02 literally says 'a shareable link AND/OR email', so both channels are in scope. Peerspace/Partiful lean on one broadcast link; Eventbrite/Google Calendar use per-recipient email invites. A crypto-random token pattern already exists (src/lib/booking/reference.ts) — but an invite token is a real ACCESS TOKEN (like the booking's opaque UUID id), not a friendly label.

options.label: Both — one shareable link + targeted email invites (recommended)
options.description: One reusable group link to drop in a chat, PLUS tokenized invites to specific emails. Matches GROUP-02's 'and/or' exactly.

options.label: Shareable link only
options.description: One link, anyone who opens it can RSVP. Lowest build cost; can't target a person or tell invited-vs-found-the-link.

options.label: Per-email tokenized invites only
options.description: Each attendee gets their own scoped token by email. Max control + you know who's invited; no 'share in the group chat' path.

questions.title: What an RSVP captures (attendee identity)
questions.context: GROUP-03 requires RSVP 'without a full account'. Resend send(to,...) takes ANY email, so emailing non-account attendees works today. BUT the in-app notification row is keyed on recipientId = user.id, so a no-account attendee gets EMAIL only. Capturing email also enables a confirmation + reminder, and is the identity a future per-attendee payment attaches to.

options.label: Name + email (recommended)
options.description: Enables confirmation email, reminder, de-duping, and is the identity hook the paid version reuses. Slight friction vs name-only.

options.label: Name only
options.description: Lowest friction, purely informational. Can't email them, can't de-dupe, no identity for the paid version.

options.label: Name + email, auto-link if logged in
options.description: Like (a), plus attach user.id when the attendee is a signed-in FitOut user so they also get in-app notifications.

questions.chat_more: RESOLVED (2026-07-27) = HYBRID guest-or-login, one rsvp row with nullable user_id. Login/sign-up -> account-linked (in-app + email, verified identity). Guest -> self-typed name + OPTIONAL email: blank = headcount-only, no comms (can't toggle, no cancellation notice; organizer's chat covers them); email given = RSVP confirmation + cancellation notice + a self-serve manage link to change the answer, NO reminders. GROUP-03 stays unchanged (guest path = no account needed). v1 simplifications: no guest email verification, no guest->account merge, opt-in email guard (only email addresses submitted via an RSVP on the link, rate-limited); de-dup by user_id / normalized email.

questions.title: Can an attendee change their RSVP after submitting?
questions.context: Plans change; Partiful/Meetup let attendees toggle freely until the event. Interacts with the cap (Q-09): a yes->no frees a spot, a no->yes must re-check the cap atomically.

options.label: Yes — can toggle yes/no until RSVP closes (recommended)
options.description: Attendee can change their answer before the RSVP close time (Q-12). A no->yes re-competes for a spot under the atomic cap.

options.label: No — RSVP is final once submitted
options.description: Simpler state, no re-cap logic. But a misclick or changed plan is stuck, and the count overstates who's coming.

questions.title: Can one RSVP bring +guests?
questions.context: Eventbrite/Evite allow 'RSVP + N guests'. This changes cap math (Q-08): if allowed, the cap counts heads not RSVPs, and a no-account +guest has no identity. One-person-one-RSVP keeps count = number of 'yes' rows.

options.label: One RSVP = one person, no +guests (recommended for v1)
options.description: Cap = count of 'yes' RSVPs. Cleanest to hard-cap atomically. '+guests' becomes a deferred idea for the ticketing version.

options.label: Allow +N guests per RSVP
options.description: 'me + 2'. More realistic for casual groups, but the cap must count heads and those extras have no identity.

questions.title: Where/how the organizer starts a group
questions.context: /bookings/[id] already exists, and /bookings/[id]/cancel is a precedent for a nested action route under a booking. The goal says the organizer 'HAS PAID' then invites — pointing at the confirmed-booking surface, not checkout. No group/invite/rsvp routes exist yet.

options.label: 'Invite people' on the confirmed booking detail page (recommended)
options.description: Every confirmed booking gets an 'Invite people' affordance that turns it into a group. Zero checkout changes; matches 'wraps a booking already paid for'.

options.label: Opt-in at checkout ('booking for a group?')
options.description: Flag 'group' during checkout. Sets intent early, but adds a branch to money-critical checkout and can't retrofit an existing booking.

options.label: Both — a checkout nudge + the post-booking affordance
options.description: Most discoverable; most surface area to build and keep consistent.

questions.title: Which bookings qualify to become a group?
questions.context: The goal says the organizer 'has PAID' — a confirmed booking. Request-to-book only reaches 'confirmed' after approval + payment, so 'confirmed' naturally covers both modes.

options.label: Any confirmed (paid) booking (recommended)
options.description: If confirmed, the organizer paid, so it can host a group — instant or request alike. Simplest rule, matches the goal.

options.label: Confirmed AND future only
options.description: Also require the session hasn't started/ended — no inviting to a past session. (a) plus the RSVP-close rule (Q-12) may already cover it.

options.label: Restrict by mode or space type
options.description: e.g. only instant-book, or only whole-space (unitCount=1). Adds guardrails but narrows the differentiator without a clear reason yet.

questions.title: When does RSVP close?
questions.context: booking.startsAt/endsAt are venue-local timestamptz. Closing RSVP bounds the cap race and stops late confusion. The reminder (Q-15) and 'who's coming' view (Q-16) key off this.

options.label: At session start (recommended)
options.description: Open from creation until the session starts, then locks. Simple; the headcount is final exactly when it matters.

options.label: A cutoff before start (e.g. 2h / 24h before)
options.description: Gives a firm number ahead of time. Requires choosing the offset; can frustrate last-minute joiners.

options.label: Never closes until the session ends
options.description: Walk-ins can RSVP after start. Most permissive; headcount never finalizes.

questions.title: What happens to invites/RSVPs if the booking is cancelled or refunded?
questions.context: Phase 7 shipped booker + host cancellation with refunds + durable notifications. 'Yes' attendees planned around this session; Partiful/Eventbrite notify attendees on cancellation.

options.label: Auto-void invites + email attendees it's cancelled (recommended)
options.description: Invites stop accepting RSVPs and every 'yes' attendee gets a cancellation email. Honest; reuses the notify/email layer.

options.label: Silently void — link shows 'no longer available', no message
options.description: Invites become inert; attendee finds out only if they revisit. Less email; leaves people uninformed.

questions.title: Can the organizer manage invites (revoke / remove / resend)?
questions.context: Guest lists change. Revoking a tokenized invite invalidates that token; removing a confirmed attendee frees a capped spot (Q-09). Regenerating the shareable link handles 'the old link leaked'.

options.label: Yes — revoke, remove attendee, resend/regenerate link (recommended)
options.description: Full control from the group view. Removing a 'yes' frees a spot atomically. More UI + actions, but expected of a coordination tool.

options.label: Minimal — resend only, no revoke/remove
options.description: Can re-share but can't kick someone or kill a leaked link. Less to build; weaker control.

options.label: None — fire-and-forget invites
options.description: Cheapest; no recourse for a wrong invite or a leaked link.

questions.title: Do attendees get a pre-session reminder?
questions.context: Phase 7 runs an at-most-once reminder cron (src/inngest/functions/reminders.ts, UNIQUE(booking_id, kind)); an attendee reminder extends that pattern. Requires attendee email (Q-02 a/c).

options.label: Yes — 'yes' attendees get a pre-session reminder email (recommended)
options.description: Reuse the reminder infra to email confirmed attendees before the session. High value; low cost. Needs attendee email.

options.label: No attendee reminders in v1
options.description: Only the organizer (a real account) gets reminders. Less to build; attendees may forget.

questions.title: What does an attendee see about the booking?
questions.context: listing.showExactAddress (D-09, default approximate) governs how much address the PUBLIC sees; neighborhood is the approximate anchor. An RSVP'd attendee is more trusted than a browser but may be a no-account stranger with a link. GROUP-04 is the ORGANIZER seeing who's coming; this is the reverse.

options.label: Name + date/time + address per showExactAddress (recommended)
options.description: Respect the host's exact-vs-approximate setting, consistent with the public listing page. Organizer can share the precise address out-of-band.

options.label: Always show the exact address to a 'yes' attendee
options.description: They're confirmed coming, so give the full address. Convenient; overrides the host's approximate-address preference for anyone with a link.

options.label: Minimal — name + time only; organizer shares location
options.description: Invite is just 'you're on the list'. Most privacy-preserving; least useful standalone.

questions.title: Notifications: organizer updates + attendee confirmations
questions.context: GROUP-04 wants the organizer to see 'headcount and who is coming' — a live view and/or a push. fitout/notify gives the organizer (a real user) in-app + email; a no-account attendee gets EMAIL only. New notification_type enum values are compile-checked in schema.ts.

options.label: Organizer notified per RSVP + attendee gets a confirmation email (recommended)
options.description: Each yes/no pings the organizer (in-app + email); each attendee gets an RSVP confirmation email. Closes the loop both ways; reuses infra.

options.label: Live headcount view, no per-RSVP push
options.description: Organizer sees the count/list on opening the group page; not pinged each RSVP. Quieter; less real-time. Attendee still confirmed.

options.label: Digest — one summary (e.g. at RSVP close)
options.description: Batch updates into one message. Least noise; least immediacy.
